transfer.title: İran'dan flaş açıklama! 'ABD ile arabuluculuk çabaları sürüyor'
transfer.summary: İran devlet televizyonuna göre, Tahran'da basın toplantısı düzenleyen İçişleri Bakanlığı Sözcüsü Zeynivend, ABD ile İran arasındaki diplomatik sürecin aracısı Pakistan'ın İçişleri Bakanı Nakvi'nin Tahran ziyaretine ilişkin soruyu yanıtladı. 'BÜYÜK BİR GAYRETLE SÜRÜYOR' Pakistan'ın arabuluculuk rolünün ve diplomatik girişimlerin "büyük bir gayretle" sürdüğünü aktaran Zeynivend, "Sorunları çözmek ve İslamabad Mutabakat Zaptı'na dönmek için uluslararası diplomatik çabalar ve arabuluculuk hala devam etmektedir." ifadelerini kullandı. 'ANLAŞMANIN HÜKÜMLERİNE UYULMALI' "Birçok ülke sorunu çözmek ve tarafları yeniden anlayışa getirmek için çaba sarf etmektedir." diyen Zeynivend, 17 Haziran'da Pakistan'ın arabuluculuğunda İran-ABD arasında imzalanan ancak uygulanmayan mutabakata işaret ederek şunları aktardı: "Karşı tarafın imzasının itibarına değer verip anlaşmanın hükümlerine uyması gerekiyor. ABD, İslamabad mutabakatının maddelerine bağlı kalmalıdır. Mutabakat Zaptı, İran'ın üst düzey bir kararıdır ve liderlik tarafından onaylanmıştır. Talebimiz, karşı tarafın bu mutabakata geri dönmesidir." ABD ile İran arasındaki diplomatik sürecin aracısı Pakistan'ın İçişleri Bakanı Muhsin Nakvi'nin birkaç gün içinde yeniden Tahran'ı ziyaret edeceği bildirilmişti. Avrupa'da tehlike sinyali! transfer.title: Brentford blitz Chelsea as Fábio Carvalho caps stunning second-half display
transfer.summary: Those early-season thoughts that Chelsea might be the team best-placed to challenge Arsenal are beginning to look extremely over-optimistic. The two chaotic wins with which they began were always difficult to read: they might have been useful points picked up on the way to a more solid structure, or they might have represented evidence of significant problems. After three games without a win, and 12 goals conceded in five games this season, it’s beginning to look like the latter. At the final whistle, Keith Andrews tipped his head back and roared at the sky, celebrating Brentford’s first home win over Chelsea since 1938. They remain unbeaten, coherent and disciplined, and moved up to third in the table. The comparison is impossible not to draw: as one side flail in an orgy of structured spending, their far less wealthy neighbours thrive with a clear plan and sense of direction. “It was a performance I felt was bubbling,” said Andrews. “I could see it in the players’ eyes over the last two days. They were very focused, very determined.” Continue reading...

worldcup.title: ‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football culture
worldcup.summary: Head coach says he must accept lack of control in games ‘Deep down, English players … they go for it’ Thomas Tuchel has admitted there are times when he craves greater control in matches. But the England head coach feels the more chaotic, adrenaline-fuelled nature of the Premier League will remain his template as he targets glory at Euro 2028. Tuchel described his team as “maybe not the most economical to play football” in terms of their habit of constantly playing at full throttle. They lost to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in July when they had nothing left in the tank and watched the game slip away after going 1-0 up in the 55th minute. England barely touched the ball thereafter, had no control and were reeled in, Argentina winning with two late goals. Continue reading...

worldcup.title: Tuchel should listen to ‘the 0.1%’ and learn from England’s World Cup mistakes | Jacob Steinberg
worldcup.summary: Head coach is keen to focus on positives but Nations League squad hints at desire for greater tactical options Thomas Tuchel should be listening to the 0.1%. As he unveiled his first England squad since the World Cup, he said 99.9% of supporters he bumped into did not talk about his substitutions during the Argentina game. According to him, the conversation is far more positive. Memories are shared of the knockout wins over Mexico and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It seems those who want to take the England head coach to task over the retreat in the semi-final in Atlanta are in the minority. This is, of course, hard to quantify. Is it really 99.9%? We can take Tuchel at face value, but relying on anecdotal evidence goes two ways. A lot of fans are not ready to move on yet. The national mood is far more downbeat than Tuchel imagines and he is kidding himself if he thinks people have forgiven the way England folded after going 1-0 up against Argentina early in the second half. Continue reading...

magazine.title: Harry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th game
magazine.summary: Striker’s double helps Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0 Dieter Müller’s record of 129 games had stood since 1977 Harry Kane broke the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 victory on Friday over Union Berlin, his 98th league game for the club. Cologne’s Dieter Müller set the previous mark in 1977, but it took him 129 matches and with the England captain scoring at better than a goal a game Kane setting the record had been inevitable for some time. Since his arrival, in 2023, Kane has scored 152 goals in 154 appearances in all competitions, including 61 in 51 games last season. Continue reading...
